snippet.title: Gary Oldman gets emotional talking about his friend John Hurt - Table Manners Podcast
snippet.description:
This week we’re joined by British acting royalty - in every sense of the word - it’s the newly knighted Sir Gary Oldman! Mum & I popped over to the Dorchester in London where Gary treated us to his (and Jackson Lamb’s) very favourite Chinese meal. We heard all about Gary living in Palm Springs, the meals his mum would cook as a child, growing up in New Cross, playing Lee Harvey Oswald in JFK, living in an empty hotel during lockdown, the future of Slow Horses, and we hear an incredibly touching story of his friendship with the late John Hurt. Thank you Gary for such a delightful afternoon, what a treat to eat and chat with such an icon. The new fifth series of Slow Horses is now streaming on Apple TV+.

Follow Table Manners on Instagram, TikTok, Facebook & X - ‪@TableMannersPodcast‬

snippet.title: What was Severus Snape really like when the cameras stopped rolling? 🪄❤️ #shorts #usa #america
snippet.description:
It turns out Hogwarts’ most stern Potions Master had a heart of pure gold behind the scenes. 🧪✨

Gary Oldman (who played Sirius Black) shared a heartwarming reflection about his late co-star Alan Rickman. While Rickman played the dark, intimidating Severus Snape on screen, off camera he regularly invited children from local schools and hospitals to visit the Harry Potter film sets to experience a bit of real-world magic. 🏰🪄

Pure Kindness: Using his platform and influence to create unforgettable memories for young fans facing difficult times. 💫

The Ultimate Contrast: Playing one of cinema’s most complex anti-heroes while being known as one of the kindest actors on set. 🎭🖤

Alan Rickman comenzó estudiando diseño gráfico y tipografía. Actuaba habitualmente, eso sí, en funciones teatrales que se montaban en la Chelsea College Of Art donde estaba matriculado. Sin embargo, poco a poco, la posibilidad de convertirse en actor, que en un primer momento había descartado por completo, fue ganando enteros y con 25 años se incorporó a la Royal Academy Of Drama Art de Londres. “Afortunadamente no era el más viejo de la escuela”, dice con sorna. Fue, sin duda, una decisión acertada porque este actor londinense es uno de los rostros más reconocidos del cine, el teatro y la televisión británicos.
